Playbook (accumulated from past tasks):
## strategies
[ace-0002] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: When a repo has a money helper module (e.g. ledgerly/money.py with to_money/round_money/ZERO), read it first and reuse its helpers for conversions, zero constants, and rounding rather than raw Decimal arithmetic.
## common_mistakes
[ace-0003] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: Returning an unrounded Decimal division for a money value (e.g. weighted average) fails review; wrap the final monetary result in round_money and return the shared ZERO constant for empty/degenerate cases.
## domain_facts
[ace-0001] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: In ledgerly, all monetary results must be rounded via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); Python's round() and bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.

item.content: When validating an integer parameter (e.g. quantity), reject bool explicitly (isinstance(x, bool)) before the int check, since bool is a subclass of int and True/False would otherwise pass as 1/0.

Reuse the existing error type and code conventions from sibling functions (e.g. BillingError with codes like invalid_state) by reading neighboring functions in the same module before implementing a new one, so validation errors match the repo's established codes.
Forgetting to enforce state guards (e.g. only draft invoices may be modified) on new mutating functions; check the status field and raise the repo's invalid_state error before mutating.
